title: Fueling Basics

learn.summary: You don't need a diet overhaul to support training — you need adequate protein, real hydration, and sensible timing. This is education, not prescription: individual needs vary, and anyone with medical conditions should talk to a professional. But the fundamentals below cover 90% of what active people get wrong.

do: Log everything you eat for just 3 days (photos are enough) — not to judge, but to see your actual protein and water baseline.

children.title: Protein Targets

learn.summary: The RDA of 0.8 g/kg is a floor to prevent deficiency, not a target for people who train. Research on active adults consistently supports 1.4–2.0 g per kg of bodyweight daily — roughly 100–140 g for a 70 kg person — spread across 3–4 meals of 25–40 g each. Muscle protein synthesis responds best to that per-meal dose, especially with training and with age.

do: Calculate your target (bodyweight in kg × 1.6 g), then build one go-to breakfast containing at least 30 g protein and eat it 3 times this week.

children.title: Hydration

learn.summary: Even 2% dehydration measurably degrades endurance and cognition. Practical markers beat formulas: pale-straw urine, and weighing yourself before and after a sweaty session — each kilogram lost is about a liter to replace. Most people need roughly 2–3 liters of total fluid daily, more in heat, with electrolytes mattering mainly in sessions over an hour or heavy sweating.

do: Fill a 1-liter bottle each morning this week with the rule: empty by lunch, refill, empty by dinner.

children.title: Eating Around Training

learn.summary: The 30-minute 'anabolic window' was oversold — total daily protein matters far more than stopwatch timing. Useful rules that survive scrutiny: a carb-containing meal 1–3 hours before hard sessions improves performance, training fully fasted is fine for easy cardio but costs quality in hard strength work, and a normal protein-containing meal within a few hours after training covers the rest.

do: Before your next hard session, eat a banana or toast 60–90 minutes prior and note whether the session feels stronger than your recent average.
